propositions: docs/releasing.md incorrectly describes the pypi environment required-reviewers rule as a 'second human approval' when it is actually a single configured identity (the release dispatcher themselves) with self-review permitted and admin bypass available

The release runbook instructs operators to 'approve the pypi deployment when prompted' as if it is an interactive UI step, but the actual approval is a non-interactive REST API call via pending_deployments that must be made explicitly

The pypi environment approval gates *identity and ref control* over who can release the publish job, not independent content review; the latter guarantee comes from Gerrit review of main, which the doc already correctly states

The pending_deployments REST API call requires a properly typed JSON body with environment_ids as an integer array, not string-typed field flags, and operators need the companion GET invocation to discover the environment id
The .github/workflows/release.yml line 294 comment repeats the 'second human gate' claim and contradicts the corrected documentation

The acceptance criteria and drift tests (test_release_workflow_pins.py) verify that corrected text removes 'second human' and 'human approval' framing and includes complete runnable REST examples with proper JSON typing
